title: How Career Centers Can Set Up & Manage Job Shadowing Programs
summary: A practical guide for college career centers to set up and manage a structured job shadowing program. Covers employer host recruitment, screening, student matching, scheduling, institutional approvals, cancellation procedures, and program evaluation.
body_markdown:
If your career center coordinates job shadowing opportunities through individual employer requests and student emails, managing placements can quickly become difficult.


Hosts need clear expectations, students need suitable matches, and staff must coordinate scheduling, institutional approvals, and last-minute changes.


A structured program replaces these one-off arrangements with a repeatable process.


Career Services teams can maintain a pool of approved hosts, establish participation criteria, allocate placements, and track completed visits without restarting coordination each semester.


This guide covers how to administer an ongoing job shadowing program, from recruiting and screening employer hosts to matching students, managing visits, and evaluating program performance.


## What Should Career Centers Establish Before Launching a Job Shadowing Program?


Career centers should first define what qualifies as job shadowing, who can participate, which activities are permitted, and how placements will be approved. Establishing these rules before recruiting hosts helps staff evaluate opportunities consistently and distinguish short-term workplace observation from internships or other work-based experiences.


### Define eligible shadowing activities


A typical placement involves observing a professional during their regular working day. Career Services should establish clear boundaries.


- **Permitted:** Observing daily responsibilities, attending approved meetings, watching demonstrations, and receiving workplace orientation.
- **Restricted:** Accessing confidential client information, patient records, proprietary materials, or controlled work areas without appropriate authorization.
- **Outside the standard scope:** Performing productive work or independently completing employee responsibilities. These activities require separate institutional review rather than automatic classification as shadowing.


### Choose between individual and small-group placements


Placement format Best suited for Administrative consideration


Individual shadowing Role-specific observation and limited-access workplaces More hosts and separate scheduling may be needed


Small-group shadowing Workplaces with capacity for multiple observers Confirm group size, supervision, and visibility of actual work


Virtual shadowing Remote roles or locations students cannot access in person Verify that students can observe genuine work activities


A small-group placement should still provide meaningful access to professional work rather than becoming a general employer presentation.


### Complete institutional reviews before confirming placements


Coordinate with the appropriate university offices to determine requirements for:


- Risk management, insurance, waivers, and site safety.
- Accessibility and reasonable accommodations.
- Student eligibility, conduct expectations, and supervision.
- Confidentiality agreements and restrictions on sensitive information.
- Transportation responsibilities and emergency contacts.


Job shadowing is one of several[career exploration activities](https://www.hiration.com/blog/career-exploration-activities-advisor-framework-higher-ed/) career centers can use to help students evaluate potential roles.


Requirements can vary by institution, host, and workplace. Career Services should document the required approvals before releasing a placement to students.


## How Can Career Centers Recruit and Screen Job Shadowing Hosts?


Recruitment should prioritize professionals who can provide an appropriate observation experience, not simply employers willing to participate. Career centers can invite[existing employer contacts](https://www.hiration.com/blog/career-center-employer-partnership-strategy-higher-ed/) , alumni professionals, and department-recommended hosts, but every opportunity should pass the same screening process before being offered to students.


### Screen hosts against a standard set of criteria


Each host registration should capture:


- Professional's name, position, organization, and primary contact.
- Job responsibilities and specific activities students can observe.
- Available dates, visit duration, location, and preferred format.
- Maximum number of students the workplace can accommodate.
- Supervision arrangements, safety requirements, and accessibility information.
- Workplace restrictions, confidentiality requirements, and necessary approvals.


Do not approve a placement solely because the employer agrees to host. A host must be able to describe what the student will actually observe.


### Job shadowing host recruitment email template


**Subject: Host a Student for a Job Shadowing Experience**


Hi \[Name\],


\[University\] Career Services is organizing short job shadowing placements for students interested in \[industry/field\].


We're inviting professionals to host a student for a \[half-day/full-day\] experience focused on observing everyday work responsibilities and understanding the role in practice.


Career Services will coordinate student matching, share participation guidelines, and support scheduling. Hosts would provide a suitable observation agenda and serve as the student's primary contact during the visit.


If you're interested, please complete our short host registration form here: \[Link\].


Thank you,
\[Name\]
\[University Career Services\]

## How Should Career Centers Match Students With Hosts and Schedule Visits?


Student-host matching should consider professional interests, available placement capacity, location, scheduling constraints, and any approved accessibility arrangements. Career centers should use consistent allocation criteria, especially when demand exceeds available placements, and confirm that both parties can meet the requirements before finalizing a match.


### Student-host matching checklist


Before approving a match, verify:


- The student's career interest aligns with the host's actual role.
- The student meets published program eligibility requirements.
- The host has an available placement within the requested period.
- The student can attend the location or approved virtual format.
- Required accessibility arrangements and institutional approvals are confirmed.
- Both parties understand the proposed duration and activities.
- The host has confirmed the student's placement.


Where applications exceed capacity, use published selection criteria and maintain a waitlist. Do not guarantee placements before confirming host availability.


### Establish a repeatable scheduling process


The[University of South Carolina's Spurs Up Shadow Program](https://sc.edu/about/offices_and_divisions/career_center/student_career_hub/gain_experience/job_shadowing/index.php?ref=hiration.com) uses separate application, matching, communication, and shadowing periods.


Career centers can follow a similarly defined sequence:


1. **Registration:** Collect host availability and student preferences within published application windows.
2. **Matching:** Allocate placements, obtain host acceptance, and notify students.
3. **Confirmation:** Finalize the visit date, duration, arrival instructions, contact information, and required documentation.


Maintain one placement tracker with the host, student, assigned staff member, scheduled date, approval status, and completion status.


## How Should Career Centers Prepare Participants and Manage Placement Issues?


Career Services should provide separate instructions to students and hosts, confirm that institutional requirements are complete, and establish a clear point of contact for problems. Standardized communication helps staff manage cancellations, unsuitable activities, safety concerns, and scheduling changes without relying on improvised decisions.


### Send separate pre-visit instructions


**Host briefing:** Confirm the observation agenda, supervising professional, permitted activities, accessibility arrangements, confidentiality restrictions, and emergency procedures.


**Student briefing:** Confirm arrival details, attendance expectations, workplace conduct, required documentation, restrictions on recording or sharing information, and whom to contact if problems arise.


The[University of Chicago's job shadowing host guidance](https://careeradvancement.uchicago.edu/student-opportunities/experiential-programs/job-shadowing-program/prospective-host-information/?ref=hiration.com) specifically addresses confidential information and the option of designing experiences around non-confidential activities.


### Establish cancellation and escalation procedures


Situation Career Services response


Host cancels before the visit Notify the student, offer an approved alternative if available, and update the placement record


Student withdraws or misses the visit Notify the host, record the reason where appropriate, and apply published rescheduling rules


Student reports unsuitable or restricted activities Review the concern, pause participation where appropriate, and consult the responsible institutional office


Safety, accessibility, or conduct concern Follow institutional reporting and escalation procedures; suspend the placement when necessary


Every host and student should know how to report concerns directly to Career Services, including during the visit.


## How Should Career Centers Collect Feedback and Evaluate the Program?


Evaluation should examine whether placements were completed, matched students appropriately, and met basic host and institutional expectations. Career centers should collect short feedback from both students and hosts, then use recurring issues to improve screening, matching, scheduling, and capacity planning for future program cycles.


### Collect post-shadowing feedback


Send separate,[brief surveys](https://www.hiration.com/blog/career-center-student-pulse-surveys-higher-ed/) after each completed placement.


**Ask students:**


- Did the activities match the role and description provided?
- Was the visit accessible, appropriately supervised, and well organized?
- Were there any problems that Career Services should review?


**Ask hosts:**


- Did the student attend and meet participation expectations?
- Was the coordination process manageable?
- Would you host another student, and what should change?


### Track program evaluation measures


Measure How to calculate or assess


Placement rate Students matched ÷ eligible student applicants


Completion rate Completed visits ÷ confirmed placements


Cancellation rate Cancelled visits ÷ confirmed placements


Match suitability Student ratings of alignment between expected and observed roles


Host retention Hosts agreeing to participate in another cycle ÷ hosts surveyed


Unmet demand Eligible students left unmatched, grouped by career field


Coordination efficiency Staff time spent per completed placement


Review unmatched demand alongside host capacity. If healthcare students consistently remain unmatched while other fields have unused placements, recruitment for the next cycle should address that specific shortage.


Similarly, repeated cancellations, unclear observation agendas, or accessibility concerns should trigger adjustments to host screening and placement procedures.


Essential checks for host recruitment, student matching, & program evaluation


## Wrapping Up


A successful job shadowing program requires consistent host screening, student matching, institutional coordination, and evaluation.


Once these processes are established, career centers can focus on improving placement quality and addressing unmet student demand.
